properties.name: Central American Dry Corridor Zone
properties.principle: Climate: the dry tropical belt of Central America's Pacific side, where the mid-summer drought (canícula) and El Niño years bring recurring drought. The extent is FAO's 2012 survey for Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras and Nicaragua (surveyed: dry months x rainfall x Holdridge life zones, in three classes of drought hazard), with Costa Rica's Guanacaste and Nicoya as an approximate extension. The lines between Sectors are ours (approximate): each FAO polygon goes whole to the Sector of the nearest named river or lake (Natural Earth 1:10m), so the lines run along FAO's own polygon edges, between the Chixoy and Cuilco, the Motagua, the Lempa and Paz, the Choluteca and San Miguel, the Ulúa, Humuya, Aguán and Patuca, the Coco, Matagalpa and Tuma, and the lakes and the San Juan; in Nicaragua the line is the edge of the Depression. Rivers Natural Earth lacks are listed in measures.

declared.name: Nicaragua-Costa Rica border
declared.note: The line between the Nicaraguan Pacific Depression and Guanacaste and Nicoya is the Nicaragua-Costa Rica border, where FAO's 2012 survey stops (its Costa Rican polygons are slivers along the border). The dry Pacific lowland runs on across it from Rivas to La Cruz: the line is an artefact of the survey, not a climatic boundary. The two Sectors share it exactly; no band is drawn.

properties.name: Guatemalan Highland Dry Valleys
properties.character: Rain-shadow valleys of the upper Chixoy (Salamá, Rabinal, Cubulco) and of the Selegua and Cuilco, draining to the Gulf of Mexico. FAO 2012 drought hazard: 2% severe, 32% high, 67% low.

properties.name: Gulf of Fonseca and Choluteca
